steps.b:
An atom has a tiny nucleus (jezgro) with protons (p⁺, charge +1) and neutrons (n⁰, no charge). Around it move electrons (e⁻, charge −1).

A proton and a neutron each have a mass of about 1 u; an electron is about 1836 times lighter, so almost all of an atom’s mass is in the nucleus.

If the atom were a football stadium, the nucleus would be a pea on the center spot and the electrons would be flies in the stands.

Atomic number Z (redni broj) = number of protons. It decides which element it is: every atom with 6 protons is carbon.

Mass number A (maseni broj) = protons + neutrons.

n = A − Z

A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons. We write it as ᴬX with Z below, for example ²³Na with Z = 11: 11 p, 12 n, 11 e.

Ions (joni) form when atoms lose or gain electrons — protons never change in chemistry.

  • Lose electrons → positive cation: Na → Na⁺ (11 p, 10 e).
  • Gain electrons → negative anion: Cl → Cl⁻ (17 p, 18 e).

Isotopes (izotopi) are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons: ¹²C and ¹⁴C both have 6 protons, but 6 and 8 neutrons.

The relative atomic mass in the periodic table is a weighted average: chlorine is about 75% ³⁵Cl and 25% ³⁷Cl, so Ar(Cl) ≈ 35.5.

Geology link: ¹⁴C and other unstable isotopes are used to date rocks and fossils.

s: The charge 3+ means 3 electrons were lost: 26 − 3 = 23.
